title: Route engine process isolation by measured request shape instead of a global default

source.title: RTX 5090 vLLM V1 multiprocess versus in-process paired reproduction
source.claim_scope: On clean vLLM main commit 613ab20f and one RTX 5090 with Qwen3.5-0.8B GPTQ, offline B=8 decode improved 1.0376x and 1.1039x in paired repeats (1.0708x pooled) when the EngineCore subprocess boundary was removed. B=1 improved only 1.0173x, below the 1.02 material floor. Correctness passed a preregistered reciprocal top-5 logprob oracle. An older guarded worktree had shown a larger 1.1175x conservative B=8 result and a B=1 regression, demonstrating version sensitivity.

problem_signatures: millisecond inter-kernel gaps aligned with decode steps

implementation_recipe: Measure the single-stream kernel-active fraction and inter-step gaps in the exact workload before changing kernels.
Compare process-isolated and in-process execution with identical model, scheduler, graph and sampling settings.
Treat process placement as a deployment-level route keyed by the frozen service shape, never as an unconditional default.
If an upstream code change is needed, preserve an explicit isolation mode and avoid selecting from a single synthetic batch.
validation_recipe: Use fresh caches and a balanced arm order so compilation and run position cannot favor one engine mode.
Report each workload separately; require paired end-to-end speedup above the material floor.
When exact greedy output is nondeterministic, preregister and apply the project's existing top-k logprob comparator rather than inventing a post-hoc tolerance.
Include low-concurrency counterexamples and reject global enablement when the direction reverses.
Reproduce on a clean upstream build before packaging a change.
expected_bottleneck_shifts: Removing an EngineCore process boundary can shorten GPU-idle gaps between decode kernel bursts.
At low concurrency, lost overlap or changed thread/process placement can dominate and reverse the gain.
After orchestration overhead falls, output projection or quantized backbone kernels may regain enough wall share to cross the Amdahl materiality gate.
failure_modes: A profiler API wait is treated as removable CPU self-time even though it includes GPU dependency waiting.
One favorable batch is used to make in-process execution the global default.
Multiprocess baseline nondeterminism is mistaken for candidate corruption or ignored without an independent oracle.
An existing environment toggle is presented as a new upstream optimization without a maintainable routing contribution.
Offline LLM measurements are generalized to the online API server, which uses a different process architecture.
Transport age is attributed to the frontend Python queue without an ablation; removing the SyncMPClient output thread was neutral in two paired repeats.
Forced-copy versus tracked zero-copy behavior is changed for small msgpack headers without measurement; the small-header copy ablation was also neutral in two paired repeats.
scope_limits: The clean-main positive reproduction is limited to offline B=8 decode on one model and RTX 5090; online serving was not measured.
B=1 did not cross the material floor on clean main and had regressed on the older guarded worktree, so this method requires explicit workload guards.
One evaluated recurrent-attention path did not support the required batch-invariant mode; exact bitwise validation therefore remained unavailable for that model.

The measured multiprocess output transport age was about 0.222 ms median versus 0.010 ms in-process, but two isolated subcomponent ablations did not recover it; the remaining opportunity spans the EngineCore output queue, serialization and ZMQ path.
This card guides candidate generation and routing; it is not proof that another workload benefits.

algorithmic_decomposition.baseline_dependency: Each autoregressive step crosses scheduler, engine and GPU-worker boundaries before the next step can launch.
algorithmic_decomposition.partition_axis: process-isolation overhead and overlap benefit as a function of active batch and request cadence
algorithmic_decomposition.combine_rule: Select an engine process mode only for workload regions where paired benefit remains material and all correctness guards pass.
algorithmic_decomposition.finalization: Emit a guarded route with negative boundaries; otherwise retain the process-isolated default.
algorithmic_decomposition.work_complexity: Two engine modes times the frozen workload matrix and paired repeats.
algorithmic_decomposition.span_complexity: One fresh-engine arm per process mode can run only when the target GPU is exclusively available.
algorithmic_decomposition.communication_cost: The transformation removes or retains an EngineCore IPC boundary; it does not change model tensor communication.
invariants: model weights, graph mode, scheduler configuration and sampling are identical across arms
performance and logprob correctness are measured in separate declared experiments
negative workload regions remain visible in the route
anti_patterns: optimize the largest kernel while GPU idle dominates wall time
enable uniproc globally from a high-batch result
relax correctness after seeing a token mismatch
claim online-serving benefit from offline LLM evidence

candidate_archetypes.name: guarded in-process offline engine
candidate_archetypes.template: For a frozen offline workload with repeated inter-step GPU-idle gaps, compare process-isolated and in-process EngineCore execution and retain in-process only behind a measured workload guard.

candidate_archetypes.name: retain isolation while reducing per-step round trips
candidate_archetypes.template: Use the in-process result as an upper-bound signal, then optimize the isolated client/worker round trip without changing the autoregressive dependency or output-copy lifetime.
